title: The dance contest with Sonny Allen
summary: Thomas tells of a prize contest dance where his waltz won and he made enemies, and says he mostly played for white dances.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: Played contest? You ever had a contest?

Yeah, yeah, we had a contest. We had a contest with, uh, Sun Allen. We had this contest with Sun Allen. Well, I tell you, how we come to have this contest, we used to rehearse them. And, uh, so some of the boys heard our band, you know, say, Man, I say, I heard a band, man. I say, I hear the band, rehearse it all the time. He said, Well, a good band. You know, tell, other fellas, tell the other fellas back, you know. Ah, man, them fellas can't play nothing. That's what the other fellas said. I say, All right. I say, Now listen. So he told them, say, Well, all right. You think they can't play nothing? I say, I tell you what you do. Put some money down there and we'll give a dance. You know what I mean? Contest, back in the turtle bag, back there, you see? It's all right. Sure enough, they all got together and put the money together. Well, you must have advertised that about a month or so, or two. You know what I mean? And, uh, so that night, when the dance came off, you see? We had people like that in. All from old river, everybody. So, Sonny Allen, he had the regular bandstand, you know, to the back. And we had to build an extra bandstand to the door. You know, the entrance where you come in. So, it's all right. We play, so. So, now we, see we have to play a number, a prize number. See? So, this man playing bass with an old man, call him Wushong. He said, he said, Sonny Allen, you know something different? I said, yeah, I know something different. I said, yeah, I know something different. I used to play a waltz when I was in the country. I was playing with a band on this side of the river, after I left on the other side, you see? Red Devil, you see? So, and we used to play these waltz all the time, you know? So, I remember, I said, yeah, I said, I'm going to play that. He said, you play it. So, I played it. So, after I played it, everybody, oh man, everybody's talking about that pretty waltz. Woo! He said, that's the beautiful waltz we'll be hearing. It's all right. So, now, when we ended, that was supposed to be a prize. So, look, everybody clapped for applause, you know? So, the police were there. So, the police were there. They still, they still, the ball band standing. So, they didn't want to give me the prize, you know? They don't want to give it to them. But the police would say, oh yeah, you can give that for that prize. They said, because he wanted fair, you know what I mean? So, and from that, from that day on, I made enemies. In the island, they wouldn't hire me no more. They wouldn't hire me no more. But, but I, most of my playing was, most of white. All my playing. Most, now most of the time I would play for color, like in Lent. See, like net, like it's net now.
And brass bands too though. Yeah, brass bands too, yeah.
Played a few parades and things. But, most I played for color, in Lent, you know. And, play all of them in the world.
